_comment: PRIOR ART: scripts/analysis/cluster-books.py — clusters whole books, not passages about one person. One entry per figure: prefix = the full-text prefix searched in pages_en (prefix*); name = the regex that names him in a sentence; out = where the page data is published; minCluster/minSamples = HDBSCAN settings for the theme map (about passages/250, floor 10). setAside = passages whose book title matches `titles` and text matches `text` (both default to anything), and whose text does not match `unless`, are given a fixed theme before clustering: they name someone else, or the figure as a fictional speaker. rare = settings for rare.py: skipTitles/skipText drop passages that are about someone else, notes attach a sentence where a passage means something other than it seems. diels = the figure's chapters in Diels, Vorsokratiker 3rd ed. 1912 (book 6a3f0220661123baf6fe9d4e) for diels.py: ch = 1912 chapter, dk = the Diels-Kranz chapter it became (44 and 47 checked in #7097; 14 and 58 by name), pages, start/end = the heading lines that open the chapter and the next one. dielsMatch = diels.py: in = [margin, raw] a passage needs to be tagged (read by band; see diels.py), hop = how close a passage must be to a tagged one to inherit its tag, judgeTop = how many repeated claims go to the reader.

notes.note: In the papers of the Bavarian Illuminati members wrote under classical code names; this Pythagoras is one of them, not the philosopher.

notes.note: Ismaël Boulliau published a book of his own titled Philolaus (1639), arguing that the earth moves; this passage is about that book, not the ancient Philolaus.
This is Philolaus the younger, a speaker in Johann Reuchlin’s dialogue On the Art of the Kabbalah (1517).
